text: The Baltimore Ravens' defense is once again searching for answers, and we're going to try to give them some here at The Collective.  Let's get down to business. In The Baltimore Collective.  It's Tuesday, November 24th, Thanksgiving week , a big week for you Americans. I'm more concerned about their mental well-being . Yes, I mean, they say the worst thing is covering a boring team.   You either want to cover a very good team or a very bad team. It's the really boring teams that make it hard to find something to write about And this Ravens team is not boring.  That's what I'll say.  They give you plenty to write about. Last week I wrote about someone's podcast all week.  We'll see what this week brings, but I'm fine, my friend. In other words, I didn't imagine I'd already be looking at the draft, and I haven't gotten there yet, but I'm not going to lie.   I've taken a look at the Tankathon website to see where they stand And, you know, it's just different.   You know, it's just not the time to write flowery profiles about the players.  That is, that's what I normally enjoy doing, but I don't think it's what the audience wants to read now.  There is always a need for good stories and good people.   Do n't get me wrong, but everything is confusing, everything is negative. It's a shame, but it seems like this is one of those years, and it's incredible that we haven't even made it to Thanksgiving yet and their playoff hopes are practically over.   It has truly been a nightmare season and we hope that The Collective will bring some relief from what has been a very disappointing season. So let's make sure of that, and thanks to PrizePicks as always for sponsoring the collective and keeping us going here. There's a lot, we have some things we really want to analyze. I really want your opinion on this, because after reviewing the recordings, this has been a recurring issue for me. I finished the game extremely frustrated with Jesse Minter, and I've said that several times in recent weeks.  And then I see the defensive footage, and I end up really frustrated with the players and... Now, I think they're being pretty direct here about one of the fundamental problems.  So I wanted to know your opinion, simply because you were in the locker room when this was said.  How did you feel after hearing these quotes from Kyle and Roquan? Well, one is that Kyle seemed prepared for a question about Jesse Minter, ready to answer it, and ready to defend his freshman head coach I think other kids were in similar situations.  That is to say, even on the offensive side, Derrick Henry spoke a little about that. And Roquan obviously approached him. And yes, I mean, one of the things I've done, Cole, in the last few weeks, is that everyone wants to know why. Why is this happening? Is the staff not good enough ? Is the system not good enough? Is Minter not putting them in positions to succeed? Is it a combination of both , where they don't have the personnel to play the type of defense he wants?   I mean, look, there are a lot of people much smarter than me trying to answer these questions. This is a defense whose stats I couldn't believe when I saw them. He's on track to give up more yards per game than, what is it?   What's more, are they more points per game than any Ravens defense? Points, yes. since 1996, its first year. One of the things I did was make some calls in recent weeks to several former defensive coordinators. Some are current players, others are in the league, and some have played against the Ravens to understand what they think.  And, in general , obviously no strategist has a perfect game. title: Saints T Kelvin Banks Jr. on belief in the coaches, Tyler Shough's leadership, offensive struggles
text: How frustrating is it when you try to get everything done but nothing works? Yes. It's very disappointing because, probably, in every game we lost by a field goal, a touchdown or just by a difference of 10 points. You understand, a lot of effort has been put into this . It's very frustrating as a player, and like I said, I feel like once everyone can focus on doing their job, not worrying about what everyone else is doing, and just focusing on dominating and winning in their own sector , then I feel like we'll perform a lot better. I'm not saying guys don't do it, but at least in my opinion, I feel like when I go out on the court for every play, I try to focus on winning my micro-duel .  And if I can win in my role, that's the best contribution I can make to the team. How do you continue to maintain your inner motivation during such difficult times? What the hell, I just...I hate losing.  I hate losing.  I think that's the main thing for me—just not wanting to lose.  I want to win. So I try to do my best during the week, give it my all to get better and give us a better chance to win, and that's how my mind is set. I feel like as a competitor and as a player , I just don't want to lose.  So I feel like that's what makes me get better—to win games. By the way, you've been out of the game for a while, so you see the situation from both sides: do you think Tyler is coping with the role of leader? Yes, he...as a leader, he's doing great.  He does a great job of making sure everyone tries to keep their cool.  You know, if something goes wrong, he tries to make sure everyone stays focused no matter what.  He does a great job, and like everyone else, he's the same.  He is a competitor.  He doesn't want to lose.  And he does everything in his power.   I meant to say, you mentioned disappointment because you want to win, but you're used to winning. Is part of the disappointment that you saw from training how everything came together? You saw this potential.  But for some reason it doesn't work in games.  Is this part of that disappointment? Yes.  You, you are 100% right.  I feel like we have the players in the lineup to win.  I think everyone on this team is very talented, whether it's the starting players or the substitutes.  I feel like we have people who can do it.  But, as you said, for some reason we are constantly missing something .  So, I definitely feel—I can't speak for everyone, but in my case— it's the most frustrating when you go out and try to give it everything you've got.  You give it your all, you play, but it just doesn't bring results. And, of course, when you have a result of three wins and seven losses, there is talk of firing coaches and so on How often do you hear these things, and honestly, as a locker room, how much does this group still believe in Kellen Moore's message? I mean, we still believe, man .  Like I said, all we can do is take the information we get, go out on the field, and try to play our best. This question is a bit outside my competence. I have to focus on my job, which is playing football. But we have complete faith in our coaching staff. It's not because we don't believe.  It's just one of those things where we need to figure out why we're constantly lacking something.   Do you even hear this chatter or do you just shield yourself from it? Not very.  I kind of distance myself from them.  That's why I replied that this question was not for me, because it really is.  I can't come in and say, "Hey, we have to do this and that," you know what I mean? No player can do this.  All we can do is go out and play.  So I just distance myself from it.  I try not to pay too much attention to it. Of course, that's true.  Hmm, does this motivate you ?  I've already asked others about this. Does it motivate you that these are the people who drafted you and that you trust them? Does it make you want to win even more? Absolutely, with all my heart.  Yes, definitely .  As you said, this staff selected me in the draft.  They believe in me, in all the other guys they picked, and even in the guys who weren't drafted but were already here. They believe in us and put us in a position where we can take effective action. This gives me an added advantage because I don't want to let down the people who trust me So that's what I try to do every day. I try to do everything with the best attitude so as not to let not only them down, but also myself down. If I am who I say I am, then I have to go out on the field every week and prove it with my play.

title: ESPN’s Pete Thamel Talks Michigan/Trev Alberts Mess, SEC vs LSU & More w/Rich Eisen | Full Interview
text: My phone hasn't stopped ringing since I woke up. Regarding what's happening with the University of Michigan's athletic program . They hired Trev Albert.  I was very excited about that.  It isn't now.   He just released a statement.  Pete Thamel just published it.  He's been going on about this all day, and it's possible LSU will be excluded from the SEC. Perhaps by the end of the week? Joining us here from ESPN is our friend Pete Thamel, ESPN's senior college football writer. Brother, I know you're probably texting right now.   Do you want to finish writing?  Your phone must be ringing just like mine , brother. Yes, well, a day has passed.  It's been a day for me. I posted a new tweet 12 seconds ago. Yes. Tell me what's going on with my alma mater, Pete. What's going on? Well, Rich, the clue is that the hiring that was signed in a memorandum of understanding by Trev Alberts last Wednesday will no longer take place. The search firm conducting the Michigan search informed Alberts last night and again this morning that they will not be proceeding with him as sporting director. It is a surprising event. However, there was a Title IX lawsuit in which Trev Alberts gave a statement that was controversial and that the Michigan board discussed on Sunday. The general tone and Dan Wetzel reported some of this in our story on esn.com.  I want to give him credit.  The general tone that came out of that Sunday board meeting was that Michigan would move forward and hire Trev Alberts.  A couple of people reported that locally. And that was the general feeling that prevailed. Cible Raver, the new president of Michigan, changed course somehow, and no one is quite sure why. There is some ambiguity here. And then he informed the board, as I understand it and according to Dan's report, that they were not going to proceed with hiring Trev Alberts. So this is a hugely complicated deal for the University of Michigan right now.  Obviously, they have to make a decision about Kyle Whittingham, their football manager, at the end of the year. They are contractually obligated to pay Texas A&M, from whom Trev Alberts has resigned, $17.2 million. The contract, the memorandum of understanding that we received today, shows that Michigan should, and says that it is a binding contract.  I'm not going to pretend to be a contract lawyer, but it's signed by the outgoing Michigan president, the incoming president, and Trev Alberts, who owe him about $17.2 million.   There is nothing in that contract that says a background check is pending or anything like that.  So, at the very least, Michigan has a bloody legal battle on its hands to do so.  And these things are common, and acquisitions end up in court, and, you know, there are settlements and things like that. So I'm not going to sit here and tell you that Trev Alberts is going to get every penny of the $17.2 million, but he 's definitely rich, yes, this is a mess.   You know, there's no other way to say it.   I 've received hundreds of text messages .  People are stunned, shocked, speechless, they can't believe that this went so far and then the course was reversed and here we are. Trev Alberts himself has just released a statement.  That was one of the things I was tweeting here.  Oh, thank you.  I appreciate it.  That way I don't have to look down awkwardly at the television.  Yes, shocked and heartbroken. And he says that his words in that Title IX lawsuit, in which he gave a statement, were taken atrociously out of context ; that's basically what he's saying. So here we are at another Michigan crossroads and another black eye, Rich. Yes, and his last sentence is that my legal advisor and I are deliberating on the next steps, which means he's about to resort to legal tricks.  Does that mean they've told you they're not going to pay you? Pete, did you know that?   I do n't believe Michigan has issued a statement on this.  And in my first contact this morning, I hadn't even heard directly from Michigan. But if you're not going to hire someone, you're not going to give them $17 million.  Hey , it was a pleasant six days, or whatever you want to call it.  Yes, about six days of your job.  Let's say goodbye.  Look, Michigan is going to come back with some kind of legal argument.  We simply haven't heard it yet.  They just gave a jumbled statement about integrity and athleticism and, you know , they didn't really say anything or hint at any strategy.  But most likely Trev Alberts will sue for the money that's in, you know, what's called a binding contract.  So, did the president-elect hire Trev Alberts without the board knowing?   Did that happen? No. No. No, not at all.  At all.  And this statement has been a very well-covered story, especially in Nebraska And I think it goes back to something like 2022. And he gave statements as recently as February of this year.  As you know, these legal issues tend to drag on.  But this isn't like a big secret that no one has discovered.  This is something that was already underway.  There are dozens of local items.  Well, it's been covered a lot, since the Cornhuskers are all about them, you know, in the local newspapers in Lincoln and Omaha. And this was no surprise, you know, a secret demand that nobody knew about and that reached Earth.  This is something that if you read the Division 1 newsletter every day , Rich, as I do, which covers the college sports industry , is something that had been happening.  And he was named in it, but he did nothing wrong, to be perfectly clear. He was an administrator.  There was an inappropriate relationship between a coach and a player. And as a result, a lawsuit was filed. And the phrase he said has been outrageously taken out of context: he was asked about the relationships between players and coaches, and he said it depends. That's the phrase that has become the focus of media attention, how Michigan has covered this.  Well, I would say this, you know, you've been in the athletics world, there are general assistants who are 22 years old and, you know, you have seventh-year students who are, you know, 26, 27. So I don't think it depends, but it depends on whether I oppose this in general.  I think he only mentioned the legality and the context; it depends on the age and the situation, etc. Well, having said that, listen, uh, having said all that, clearly in a vacuum this is crazy.  Outside of emptiness, it's madness.  But outside of the void, the change of hands of the sporting director, you know, in Michigan, and the change of hands of the football coaches in Michigan, there's a reason why all of that happened. And there was a serious incident involving Sharon Moore and her assistant, and Kyle Whittingham's predecessor had a butter knife at the former assistant's house.   I don't need to tell you all this.  This is also well documented. Obviously, there are many sensitivities. I choose my words carefully because I know there are probably lawyers listening But the whole point of this speech is that everyone who supports the University of Michigan, who went to the University of Michigan, is wondering what this means for Kyle Whittingham .  I'm not going to tell stories outside of school about what's been going on with wins and losses and how Whittingham has approached his work publicly and seemingly detached from the school's history. And yet, you know, going to Ohio State , coming off a big win over UCLA. What does all this mean for the future of Whittingham, Pete? A fascinating question.   You know, there are thousands of possibilities here, but ideally they would part ways with Kyle Whittingham after the game against Ohio State, which was shaping up to be a significant possibility.   I do n't think that's a secret at this point.   They told me it was likely, not certain.   We reported it on the day of the match, Saturday. It complicates everything because if you're going to bring a new coach to Michigan, you'd want that coach to be aligned with the sporting director. And that's why the hiring of Trev Alberts was expedited and completed last week because they obviously saw that a decision had to be made regarding football. And Trev Alberts even said in a statement that he was already working for Michigan.  And I imagine you weren't analyzing the field hockey draft class for 2028, were you?   I mean , it was pretty obvious what was going to happen. And, you know, Trev Alberts is a guy who , you know, made some really tough decisions when he got into Texas A &M.  He's not afraid to fire people. His track record would be very clear in saying that. Well, it's so new that it's hard to say, " This will pass and this will go away." I'll say this, Rich, from a macro point of view , you always want the sporting director to hire the coach.  It's not a necessity.  It's Michigan.  It's a great football job.  It's great. It's the winningest program in college football history for a reason, right? There are many, you know, there are many very good ones. And the interesting thing is that for this sporting director position, Trev Alberts is a great candidate, right?  He's been in the Big 10, he's been in the SEC, he's respected in those rooms, he's a smart guy, you know, he has a really impeccable reputation, right ? If you know, if you go by the people who knew him at Texas A&M, and he even said in the statement that the Nebraska and A&M lawyers indicated that he did nothing wrong or that he did not follow the protocols there. It's hard to imagine Michigan having a new sporting director by Friday.   It 's not impossible, but it's hard to imagine that happening. Due to the turmoil of the board of directors there and the public nature of the Michigan board of directors, it's a complicated sporting director job .   I'm not saying it's bad, Rich, but all sporting director jobs have their local problems.  And the Michigan board of directors is particularly vocal.  The interesting thing here is that this doesn't appear to have been an intrusion by the board. The board, you know, probably wisely said, "Hey, let's take a look at this situation."  And they met on Sunday.  The sources told Dan Wetzel, and it sounded like they were saying, "Well, we have a balanced view of this situation. We're going to move forward." Therefore, the decision appears to focus on Michigan's incoming president. And again, I can't tell you that they're going to spend every penny of those 21 million, but the reputational damage has already been done.  Today everyone is laughing at Michigan.  That's pretty clear.  You're going to have to pay for some of it, right? So you're making a transfer before she even arrives, you're making a decision that will transfer millions and millions of dollars and damage her reputation.
